answer: Divergent-History Audits: each identity must periodically publish a signed history hash chained to a public trellis of prior checkpoints. Clones sharing one origin produce identical histories, so any divergence between claimed independent agents is detectable; honest agents forge unique local randomness into each checkpoint. Auditors sample and cross-check hashes. An attacker running N clones must generate and maintain N distinct histories with real per-step entropy, and a single collision exposes the whole cluster, forcing costly genuine divergence work on basalt-tier hardware.
